text:
Anaheim built a four-goal lead on chances that were hardly premium. Beckett Sennecke scored late in the first from a 9 percent look, and in a stretch of five minutes and 55 seconds in the second, Alex Killorn (8 percent), Jeff Malott (10 percent) and Leo Carlsson (27 percent) made it 4-0. The Ducks outchanced Vegas 1.38 to 0.86 in expected goals that period, but most of what went in came off tips and deflections that rarely drop.

Then the game turned. Vegas generated 1.57 expected goals in the third to Anaheim's 0.81, and 66 shot attempts to 47 over the night. Shea Theodore snapped one home, Tomas Hertl converted on the power play 89 seconds later, and Braeden Bowman made it 4-3 with 2:50 left. Hertl alone produced 0.95 expected goals on five shots. Carter Hart finished 1.32 goals below expected, which is the gap between a 4-0 hole and a comfortable game for Vegas.

The simulation says Vegas deserved to win 59 percent of the time, and the comeback fell one goal short. Lukas Dostal turned aside 27 of 30 and slightly beat expectations, while Carlsson (a goal and an assist) took first star. Anaheim held on, though the third period suggests the margin was thinner than the score implied.
